script: Is Manchester City really about to sign Enzo Fernández? So Chelsea just did something that almost never happens in the transfer market, because they gave Manchester City a hard deadline of 5 PM this Friday. If City don't make an offer that meets Chelsea's valuation of £120 million by then, Enzo Fernández isn't going anywhere and he stays at Chelsea with no extensions and no waiting until the window shuts on September 1st. But the fee is the part of this deal that everyone's watching for the wrong reason. Fernández has reportedly already agreed personal terms with City because he wants the move, and his old manager Enzo Maresca is now at City and wants him badly. So the player side is basically done, and the only thing left is City agreeing to pay Chelsea's price, yet Chelsea have not received a single formal bid all summer. But there's one name standing between City and this entire deal. City can't really afford Fernández until they sell somebody first, and that somebody is Rodri, who Barcelona want and who has already agreed to join them. The problem is City keep rejecting the offers since Barcelona's first bid got turned down, and their second, worth around €70 million, got rejected too, while City are holding firm at £80 million. Fabrizio Romano says those talks are in the final stretch, and City are also raising cash by selling Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi for about £60 million. So the real answer is this. It looks like that City will only sign him if they sell Rodri in the next 48 hours, because if that deal stalls, Fernández stays at Chelsea because of the deadline they created.
